services.title: Career consultation
services.text: A free session on your profile and where it can take you. We walk you and your family through Malaysian tuition, the twelve-month Graduate Pass and who is eligible for it, and the route onward to an Employment Pass, so everyone decides with the same facts.

services.title: Language test
services.sub: MUET, IELTS, TOEFL iBT, PTE, Cambridge, ELS
services.text: Training, mock tests and free study material, then a booking for a test EMGS accepts for the Student Pass. Attach the certificate to your application: without it EMGS may not grant a pass for the full length of your course. The Duolingo English Test is not on the EMGS list.

services.title: College selection
services.text: Based on your interests and marks, we compare public research universities, private universities, foreign branch campuses and university colleges. You see module structures, credit requirements, placement years and graduate outcomes before you choose.

services.title: Documentation
services.text: Samples, clear requirements and strict formatting for your statement of purpose, references and transcripts. We review everything several times before anything is submitted, which is how complicated profiles still clear.

services.title: Student Pass
services.text: Malaysia runs no credibility interview for a Student Pass, so the decisive work is on paper. We check every field of your EMGS application against your offer letter, build your financial evidence, arrange the pre-arrival medical screening, and catch the 18-month passport validity rule, the most common avoidable error.

services.title: End-to-end settlement
services.text: We map the long game: checking your nationality against the Graduate Pass list, lining up the Malaysian citizen sponsor it requires, then employer sponsorship for an Employment Pass and the route to Permanent Residence.

services.title: Financial aid
services.text: Collateral and non-collateral education loans through our banking partners, covering tuition and accommodation. Strong students get guided applications for merit scholarships and bursaries straight from Malaysian institutions.

services.title: Post-landing
services.text: Safe accommodation, the post-arrival medical screening and Student Pass endorsement, local health insurance, a Malaysian bank account and a Touch 'n Go card, and your institution's application for vacation work permission.

services.title: Family migration
services.text: Postgraduates may bring a spouse, children and even parents on Dependant Passes. Undergraduates may only do so from 17 listed countries, and India is not one of them, so we check your eligibility before you plan around it.

steps.title: Profile, shortlist and English test
steps.text: A free consultation, a realistic shortlist, and an English test EMGS accepts. Check your passport: it must be valid for at least 18 months.
steps.alt: A student talking with a counsellor

steps.title: Accept your place
steps.text: We prepare transcripts, statement of purpose and references so the offer letter and your EMGS details match exactly.

steps.title: Your institution applies, through EMGS
steps.text: EMGS processes it with your health declaration and pre-arrival medical screening. Your institution signs a personal bond with the Immigration Department on your behalf.
steps.alt: A passport on top of travel documents

steps.title: Your Visa Approval Letter arrives
steps.text: The eVAL is your permission to travel. No credibility interview is involved. We brief you on packing, arrival and campus life before you fly.
steps.alt: The view from a plane window above the clouds

steps.title: Selamat datang! Three things in week one
steps.text: A post-arrival medical screening, health insurance bought in Malaysia, and the Student Pass endorsed in your passport. We help with housing and banking too.
steps.alt: A traveller reading the departures board in an airport

steps.title: A twelve-month Graduate Pass
steps.text: A Long-Term Visit Pass after a bachelor's degree or higher, with part-time work in approved sectors. It needs a personal bond from a Malaysian citizen sponsor earning at least RM 1,500 a month.
steps.note: Open to 32 nationalities. For Indian and Chinese nationals it is decided case by case and currently authorised until 31 December 2026. We confirm the current rule before you count on it.
steps.alt: A graduate in cap and gown

steps.title: Employment Pass, then Permanent Residence
steps.text: An employer-sponsored Employment Pass for long-term work, and later an Entry Permit for Permanent Residence once you are established.
steps.alt: Two colleagues working at laptops in an office

faq.q: What do I need to apply to study in Malaysia?
faq.a: A passport valid for at least 18 months, your academic transcripts, and proof of English on the EMGS list: MUET, IELTS, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, Cambridge English or ELS. Attach the certificate to your application, or EMGS may not grant a pass for the full length of your course. Some postgraduate courses, MBAs in particular, also ask for a GMAT score or work experience.
faq.short: What do I need to apply?

faq.q: How does the Student Pass process work?
faq.a: Once you accept an offer, your institution lodges your application with EMGS, which issues the eVAL (Visa Approval Letter). You complete a health declaration and pre-arrival medical screening, and your institution signs a personal bond with the Immigration Department for you. After you land you take a second medical screening, buy health insurance in Malaysia, and Immigration endorses the Student Pass in your passport. There is no credibility interview.
faq.short: How does the Student Pass work?

faq.q: Is the Duolingo English Test accepted?
faq.a: Not for a Malaysian Student Pass. EMGS lists the tests it accepts, and Duolingo is not among them. Sitting the wrong test can cost you an intake, so we book one that is on the list.

faq.q: How much does it cost to study in Malaysia?
faq.a: Public university tuition starts from about RM 14,000 a year; private universities and branch campuses cost more, and their tuition for international students carries 6% service tax. Living costs depend heavily on the city. Use the cost planner above for an estimate, and your counsellor will build an exact figure for your offer.

faq.q: Can I work while I study?
faq.a: Not during term. You may work up to 20 hours a week during semester breaks longer than seven days, in restaurants, petrol kiosks, mini markets and hotels, and only with prior Immigration Department approval that your institution applies for.
faq.short: Can I work while I study?

faq.a: A Long-Term Visit Pass that lets you stay in Malaysia for twelve months after a bachelor's degree or higher, with part-time work in approved sectors and no employer sponsor. It is open to 32 nationalities and needs a personal bond signed by a Malaysian citizen sponsor earning at least RM 1,500 a month. For Indian and Chinese nationals it is decided case by case and is currently authorised until 31 December 2026, so we check the rule before you rely on it.

faq.q: Can my family come with me?
faq.a: Postgraduate students may apply for Dependant Passes for a spouse, children, parents and parents-in-law. Undergraduates may only do so if they are citizens of one of 17 listed countries, and India is not currently one of them.

faq.q: Do you help with accommodation and arrival?
faq.a: Yes. We work with student housing providers near your campus, run a pre-departure briefing on culture, academics, packing and immigration, and help in your first week with the medical screening, insurance, a bank account and a Touch 'n Go card.
